Selected projects

01 Sept 2025 – Mar 2026

Electric Motorsport Reduction Gearbox — Academic Project

Two-stage spur gearbox designed from scratch: 6,000 → 1,500 rpm, 400 Nm output. Sized gears via Lewis bending stress, selected SKF bearings for 9,000-hour L10 life, verified all shafts against Von Mises criterion (SF = 2). Identified 5 stress concentration failures at shoulders and keyways via Peterson factors; mitigated with relief grooves, cutting localised stress by up to 34.8% and achieving fatigue SFs of 2.0–25.1. Iterative ANSYS FEA (610k elements) drove mass optimisation; PA2200 SLS print physically tested on servo-hydraulic rig — FEA predicted 73.93 N/mm vs 83.9 N/mm measured, discrepancy explained via parametric fixture compliance study.

Lewis bending stress SKF bearing selection Von Mises criterion Peterson factors ANSYS FEA SLS printing
02 May 2025 – Present

Vibrocompliant Detangler — Personal Mechatronics Project

Custom mechatronic haircare device: vibration ERM motor integrated into a flexible TPU 95A bristle matrix, print-profiled for functional stiffness without layer sag. Arduino C++ firmware drives motor via PWM and logs strain data from an HX711 24-bit ADC at 100 Hz, with a moving-average DSP filter and auto-tare for a clean noise floor. Drop testing across PWM sweep identified an optimal band (50–75% PWM, ~40–55 Hz) that minimised peak structural deflection.

Mechatronics TPU 95A printing Arduino C++ PWM control DSP filtering HX711 ADC
03 Sept 2024 – June 2025

Medical Robotic Manipulator — Academic Project

Two-link robotic arm for remote surgical simulation. Applied inverse kinematics to verify end-effector reach at 45°, 90°, and 135° approach angles to a 330 mm target. Led full SolidWorks assembly CAD: truss-structured links for vibration damping, end effector iterated from split-clamp to friction collet after identifying long-term stress failure risk. Arduino Uno C++ firmware controls dual servos via PWM with smooth angle-sweep, joint limits, and timed motion delays.

Inverse Kinematics SolidWorks CAD Vibration damping Arduino Uno Servo PWM control
04 Apr 2026 – Present

CAD-to-AI Transcompiler — Open-Source Tool

Python/Streamlit tool that converts 3D CAD files (.STL, .OBJ) into structured JSON/CSV bundles for LLM ingestion — extracting mesh topology, bounding geometry, surface normals, principal inertia axes, and volume-to-bounding-box ratios via Trimesh and NumPy. Auto-generates a natural language geometric summary so AI can reason over engineering parts directly; includes an interactive Plotly 3D mesh viewer for real-time geometry inspection. About

I'm a third-year BEng Mechanical Engineering student at Cardiff University, predicted 1st Class Honours, with a focus on design, dynamics, and control systems.

I got into engineering because I like building things that work under pressure — from stress-testing gearbox prototypes on servo-hydraulic rigs to running vibration tests on avionics hardware. As Mechanical Lead of Avionics at Cardiff Rocket Labs, I design and test flight hardware under real mission constraints.

Beyond core engineering, I hold a Wales–Brazil British Council Research Fellowship (2026), collaborating with UFPA on flood resilience and climate adaptation in informal housing — applying structural analysis to real-world vulnerability at scale. I'm also interested in how control systems and feedback loops make physical interactions safer and more responsive.
